assessment_summary: The statement claims that for any planar graph and any proper 4-coloring of G-v (where deg(v)=5 and all 4 colors appear on its neighbors), a SINGLE Kempe-chain interchange will leave at most 3 colors on the neighbors of v. This is the false lemma from Kempe's original attempted proof of the Four Color Theorem. It was refuted by Heawood, who provided a counterexample (e.g., the Heawood graph). In such a counterexample, the neighbors of v are colored 1, 2, 3, 4, 2 in cyclic order. The 1-3 Kempe chain connecting the neighbors colored 1 and 3, and the 1-4 Kempe chain connecting the neighbors colored 1 and 4, mutually entangle and block the 2-4 and 2-3 chains of the two neighbors colored 2. Because of this, any single Kempe-chain interchange either simply permutes the colors of two connected neighbors (leaving the set of colors unchanged at 4) or changes the color of only one of the neighbors colored 2 (again leaving 4 colors in the neighborhood). Thus, no single interchange can reduce the number of colors on the neighbors to 3, making the statement false.
